newsitem.title: USA: GM earnings jump to $1.7 billion in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: GM earnings jump to $1.7 billion in first quarter.

text.p: Hailing its best North American performance in more than 10 years, General Motors Corp. said Monday it earned $1.7 billion in its first quarter, up from $714 million a year earlier.
The nation's largest automaker said it earned $2.30 a share, up from 94 cents in the first quarter of 1996, and its sales grew to $42.26 billion from $39.24 billion.
GM said its North American Operations reported net income of $764 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared with a net loss of $279 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Delphi Automotive Systems, GM's automotive parts operations, reported net income of $180 million in the first quarter of 1997, compared with net income of $79 million in the first quarter of 1996.

GM International Operations reported net income of $317 million in the latest quarter, compared with profits of $432 million in the prior-year period. The most recent quarter included a $55 million after-tax gain related to an agreement with Volkswagen A.G.
